## 🍎 Apple Silicon / local inference ecosystem

- <a id="st-5745ce974a94" class="st-a"></a>**Inference tricks built for Nvidia servers often don't carry over to a Mac.** A NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper tests four families of optimisation on four Apple machines under a single-request decoding workload, with matched RTX 4090 comparisons. KV-cache pruning reaches up to 1.75× end-to-end throughput on Apple but can reduce throughput on desktop Nvidia GPUs. Every speculative-decoding method tested made Apple decoding slower, despite reported 2–6× gains on server GPUs. CUDA kernel designs transfer only partly, because Apple's public Metal API lacks asynchronous memory copies and batch-of-one decoding makes several server mechanisms irrelevant; the parts that do transfer give up to 1.20× faster decoding. Quantization gains vary by machine. The authors conclude that a speedup belongs to the combination of technique, runtime, hardware and workload, not to the technique. For anyone running local models: benchmark on your own machine before adopting a trick. `[preprint]` ([arXiv:2610.31479](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31479) · K. Yemets, A. Yaroshevych, V. Muryn et al. (affiliation not listed))
